tasks.title: D3 + D1: correct CanvasPoint's NaN paragraph, then re-break mid-sentence /// lines in CanvasPoint, PlacedObject and ObjectKind
acceptance: D3 scope. D3's rewrite stays inside one element: the second <para> of CanvasPoint.cs's type-level <remarks> (startRef :15-26). The type-level <remarks> still holds exactly three <para> elements. Evidence: read the type-level <remarks> block.

D3 removes the false claim. The second <para> no longer says that a NaN coordinate of a CanvasPoint reaches EF, SaveChanges or a commit. At startRef :18 says it 'throws on save' as a DbUpdateException wrapping InvalidOperationException, and :25 says 'So the store stops one of three cases, at commit time'. Neither claim survives. If the paragraph names DbUpdateException, it presents EF's wrapper as no longer observable, matching CanvasPointNonFinitePersistenceTests.cs:55-62, and never as reachable. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D3 states the guard. The second <para> says that CanvasPoint's finiteness guard rejects a NaN coordinate when the CanvasPoint is created (and through the init accessors), so a NaN never reaches EF. This matches CanvasPoint.cs:53-54, :70, :82 and :106-112 at startRef. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D3 keeps the ADO-layer attribution. The second <para> still says that a NaN parameter bound through Microsoft.Data.Sqlite is refused with InvalidOperationException('Cannot store 'NaN' values.'). It still says this is the ADO provider declining to bind, not a SQLite constraint and not the IsRequired() mapping. This matches CanvasPointNonFinitePersistenceTests.cs:20-26. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D3 keeps the column-type point. The second <para> still says that the REAL column type is why a floating-point bind is attempted at all, and that a TEXT mapping would store NaN without complaint. This matches startRef :23-24 and CanvasPointNonFinitePersistenceTests.cs:26-28. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D3 keeps the asymmetry. The second <para> still says that PositiveInfinity and NegativeInfinity round-trip intact while NaN cannot be written. The third <para>, which is word-preserved, opens 'One consequence of that asymmetry' and needs that referent. This matches CanvasPointNonFinitePersistenceTests.cs:33-36. Evidence: read both paragraphs.

D3 follows the doc-comment rules (dotnet-format.md:376 and :378). Every description line (every line that is not a tag-only line such as <para> or </para>) of the rewritten second <para> holds one or more complete sentences and ends with a period. No sentence spans two /// lines. Every cref in it names a type or member that exists. The build does not check crefs, per C1 section 10. Evidence: read the paragraph and resolve each cref.

tasks.title: D2 + D4 + D6: scope Result<T>.Value's closed-construction claim, qualify Area's once-only wrapper comment, document Translate's ArgumentOutOfRangeException
acceptance: D2 scopes the claim. The second <para> of Value's <remarks> in ResultOfT.cs (startRef :36-41) no longer says, unqualified, that Result<Guid> is 'the only closed construction this application uses'. Any exclusivity claim left is scoped to production code (src/ without the test projects), or it names the survey it rests on. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D2's claim is true. Every statement the rewritten paragraph makes about which closed constructions of Result<T> exist holds when C1 section 7's S1 and S2 are rerun in the worktree. Production closes Result<T> only over Guid, directly and through ICommand<Guid>, ICommandHandler<_, Guid> and SendAsync<Guid>. The test projects also close it over int, as at DispatcherCancellationTests.cs:155. Evidence: rerun S1 and S2 and report what they print.

D2 does not falsify itself (FORM 17). If the rewritten paragraph states a command and its result, either the command's population excludes ResultOfT.cs or the result is stated as of a named commit. If no command is stated, this criterion is met by reading. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D2 keeps the paragraph's technical content. The rewritten paragraph still says that T is unconstrained, so the '?' annotation has no effect once T is closed as a value type. It still says that for Result<Guid> a failed result's Value is Guid.Empty, which cannot be told apart from a Guid a successful operation could return. Evidence: read the paragraph.

D2 follows the doc-comment rules (dotnet-format.md:376 and :378). Every description line (every line that is not a tag-only line such as <para> or </para>) of the rewritten paragraph holds one or more complete sentences and ends with a period. Every cref names something that exists, because the build does not check crefs (C1 section 10). Evidence: read the paragraph.

D2 fixes only its own paragraph's sentence breaks. P2 (C1 section 2) on ResultOfT.cs prints exactly :27, :32 and :33, nothing else. At startRef it also prints :37, :38 and :39. The three that stay are other paragraphs, out of scope and routed to the backlog. Rerun fixture1 and fixture2 (C1 section 2) in your own scratch directory first and report their outputs.

ResultOfT.cs keeps tab-indented descriptions (dotnet-format.md:375). This deliberately asserts preserved state. I1 (C1 section 4) prints nothing on ResultOfT.cs. Rerun I1's fixture first and report its output.

D4 removes the unqualified once-only claims. The // comment above _outlineView in Area.cs (startRef :12-24) no longer says, unqualified, that the wrapper is built once or at most once per Area, or that Outline returns the same instance on every read. At startRef that claim appears at :12-13 ('built once and reused, so Outline hands back the same instance on every read') and at :24 ('it is still built at most once per Area'). Each is removed, or qualified so it stays true when two threads make the first read at once. '_outlineView ??= _outline.AsReadOnly()' (Area.cs:76) is a non-atomic check-then-assign. Evidence: read the comment.

D4 adds no unverified threading claim. If the rewritten comment says how Area is accessed across threads (for example 'single-threaded, which is how the aggregate is used'), it cites the file:line evidence for that. Otherwise it makes no such claim. Evidence: read the comment.

D4 touches only that comment. The diff to Area.cs changes only lines inside the startRef :12-24 comment block. The rest of the block still carries its MASTER-114 rationale: why the wrapper cannot be built in the constructor, and the AreaOutlineChangeTrackingTests measurement. Evidence: the task diff.
